+# Incident Postmortem: High API Latency & Edge Client Request Jitter
+
+## Root Cause
+Commit `d0fabacc3eecd5f9fc2c62291f3c2c4eba0a2b4b` ("Order library list by shelf position") replaced database-level query ordering and pagination in `api/routes/books.py` with in-memory Python sorting (`sorted(books.all(), key=_rank, ...)`). For every request to `/v1/books`, the API fetched all book records from the database into memory and executed Python string operations and Unicode NFKD decomposition on every item. This bypassed the database index (`ix_books_owner_lower_title`) and database-level `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` pagination, causing CPU saturation and high request latency (p99 ~5s) on `booklogr-api`.
+
+## Evidence Used
+1. **Alertmanager Signals**: Active alerts `EdgeClientRequestJitter` ("flapping request jitter detected on edge client traffic generator") and `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` ("p99 HTTP request latency is 4.974s").
+2. **Prometheus Metrics**: `rate(flask_http_request_duration_seconds_sum[1m])` identified `/v1/books` as the primary bottleneck consuming ~4 seconds of total request duration per second.
+3. **Git History & Diff Analysis**: `git log` and `git diff` showed commit `d0fabacc3eecd5f9fc2c62291f3c2c4eba0a2b4b` replacing `books.paginate(page=offset, per_page=limit)` with `books.all()` and custom Python sorting.
+
+## What Was Changed
+- Reverted commit `d0fabacc3eecd5f9fc2c62291f3c2c4eba0a2b4b` in `api/routes/books.py`.
+- Restored SQL-level sorting (`Books.query.order_by(...)`) and database pagination (`books.paginate(...)`), leveraging the existing `ix_books_owner_lower_title` index to serve paginated library requests efficiently.
